title: Daniel Dobrygowski (Author, techgov.info · Adjunct Professor, Columbia) — 'Ries effectively broke down where corporate governance in the US has failed'
summary: Daniel Dobrygowski — technology-governance author (techgov.info), Adjunct Professor at Columbia, attorney at Sophos, and board member — publishes a substantive Incorruptible endorsement singling out the 'New Governance' chapter and connecting the book's framework to Digital Trust: multistakeholder methods for building better guardrails on innovative tech.
blockquote: I just finished Eric Ries latest book: Incorruptible: Why Good Companies Go Bad … and How Great Companies Stay Great. If you are interested in good governance and/or what makes an organization with a mission sustainable over the long term, check it out. There's a lot of great ideas and stories in the book, but I was especially excited to see his chapter on "The New Governance". Ries effectively broke down where corporate governance in the US has failed to serve the public or business leaders and what can help us govern better. The ideas in "Incorruptible" fit in incredibly well with #DigitalTrust concepts like responsible decision making for new tech and multistakeholder, interdisciplinary methods to build better guardrails for tech.
